column3: Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “You asked” to mark the quotation of God’s words.
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “You said” to mark the quotation of God’s words.
Close to the Hebrew; אֶמְאַס (“I reject, retract”) is rendered with a supplied object, “I abhor myself.”
Close to the Hebrew; נְכוֹנָה (“what is reliable”) is rendered “what is right.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I will lift up his face” is rendered “I will accept him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the LORD lifted up Job’s face” is rendered “the LORD had accepted Job.”
Close to the Hebrew; “turned the captivity of Job” is rendered “restored Job’s losses.”
Close to the Hebrew; קְשִׂיטָה (“a qesitah”) is rendered “a piece of silver,” and “evil” “adversity.”
